title: GIRL SCOUT TOP SELLER
full_story:
Girl Scouts of Southern Illinois has wrapped up the annual Fall Product Program for 2026.  Girls in Southern Illinois sold $457,000 in tasty treats, magazines, and other fun products.

Gracie Phillips from the Clay County Service Unit sold $2,319 in product to be named the Top Seller for this area.

“The Fall Product Program is a great way for girls to raise funds to launch adventures in their new Girl Scout year,” said Katie Grayling, Director of Product Programs.  “While gaining valuable life skills, girls are funding exciting opportunities where they can explore their interests, make lifelong friends, and find what’s within.  We can’t wait to see where this year takes them.”

Girl Scout Product Programs help girls gain five valuable life skills, goal setting, decision making, money management, people skills, and business ethics; that will benefit them throughout their lives.  And, proceeds from these programs stay local to provide numerous opportunities for girls to discover their strengths, develop character and resilience, and find joy in every step, all while staying true to who they are becoming.

Girl Scouts of Southern Illinois serves nearly 5,900 girls and engages over 3,250 adults in 40 counties in Southern Illinois.  Join Girl Scouts of Southern Illinois today.  Adult volunteers and girls in K-12 are welcome.  Call 800-345-6858 or email [email protected].  Girl Scouts of Southern Illinois is a not-for-profit organization supported by various United Ways, businesses, and individual donors throughout the region.

title: GATEWAY CHANGES DISINFECTANT
full_story:
Beginning Monday, November 16th Gateway Regional Water Company will begin a modified disinfection process using Free Chlorine instead of Chloramines for its predominant water disinfectant.  Beginning December 21st, they will switch back from Free Chlorine residual to the normal Chloramines residual for its predominant water disinfectant.

Customers with health issues should contact their physicians with any health-related questions.

Customers on Gateway Regional Water Company include the City of Flora; Clay County Water; Western Wayne Water Company; Village of Xenia; Village of Iuka; City of Kinmundy; Village of Alma; Village of Farina; Fayette Water Company; FMC Water Co.; NEMC Water Co.; Village of Patoka; Raccoon Water Co.; and Village of Vernon.

If you have any questions, please contact Gateway at 618-775-1004.

title: STATE CROP REPORT
full_story:
With harvest in the rearview mirror for most Illinois farmers, to-do lists are now filled with tasks preparing for the next growing season.  USDA reported 93% of corn and 96% of soybeans had been harvested across the state as of November 8th, both slightly ahead of the five-year average pace.  Winter wheat planting is also winding down with 93% complete, the USDA estimates 71% of the crop has emerged.

There were 4.8 days suitable for field work during the week ending November 8th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 53 degrees, 6.5 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 0.6 inches, 0.15 inches below normal.

Topsoil moisture supply was rated 14% very short, 30% short, 51% adequate, and 5% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 17% very short, 32% short, 47% adequate, and 4% surplus.

Corn harvested reached 93%, compared to the 5-year average of 91%.

Soybeans harvested reached 96%, compared to the 5-year average of 92%.

Winter wheat planted reached 93%, compared to the 5-year average of 89%.  Winter wheat emerged reached 71%, compared to the 5-year average of 67%.  Winter wheat condition was rated 3% very poor, 5% poor, 30% fair, 53% good, and 9% excellent.

title: FEDERAL RURAL HEALTH FUNDING
full_story:
US Representative Mike Bost Monday applauded a Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services’ announcement that Illinois will receive over $190 million in federal funding to strengthen rural healthcare systems and address workforce shortages in underserved communities.  The funding was awarded through the Rural Health Transformation Program, which Bost voted to create last year.

“The Rural Health Transformation Fund is a lifeline for Southern Illinois’ rural communities, improving patient services closer to home and providing additional support for our healthcare workers.  I proudly supported President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts law, which established this rural health fund, because we need to invest in keeping our hospitals strong and our families healthy.”

The Rural Health Transformation Program will distribute $50 billion nationwide over five years, with $10 billion awarded annually through fiscal year 2030.  This latest investment by the Trump administration brings the state’s total awards to about $384 million over two years.

title: ACE PATROL RESULTS
full_story:
Troop 9 Commander Captain Bruce Waggoner announced that Alcohol Countermeasure Enforcement, or ACE patrols, were active during October in Clay, Effingham, Lawrence, Marion, Wayne, and White counties.  The targeted patrols focus on preventing, detecting, and enforcing violations related to impaired driving and the illegal transportation or consumption of alcohol or drugs.

During the enforcement period, troopers issued two driving under the influence citations and nine other alcohol or drug-related citations.  Officers also cracked down on non-alcohol violations, recording 45 registration offenses, 41 speeding tickets, 18 driver’s license offenses, and one insurance violation.  In total, the October patrols resulted in 26 citations or arrests and 141 written warnings.

State police emphasize the importance of these details, noting that alcohol and drug impairment are estimated to be factors in over 47% of all fatal motor vehicle crashes in Illinois.  Nationally, an alcohol-related traffic fatality occurs every 39 minutes.

The ACE patrol project is funded through the Illinois Department of Transportation.

title: GET COVERED UNDERWAY
full_story:
The Get Covered Illinois 2027 annual open enrollment period is now open, helping Illinoisans compare plans, apply for financial help and enroll in coverage.  With federal changes signed into law by President Trump affecting access to affordable health insurance, the state’s official marketplace is committed to connecting Illinoisans to high-quality, affordable health coverage.

“Whether enrolling for the first time or insured for years, people deserve to understand their options and feel confident in their choice,” said Ann Gillespie, Director of the Illinois Department of Insurance.  “That’s why having a marketplace dedicated to Illinoisans matters.  We know the communities we serve, the challenges they face and the importance of having reliable health coverage.  Get Covered Illinois gives residents a trusted place to make informed decisions about their coverage.”

Open enrollment runs through January 15th, giving residents the opportunity to enroll in, renew or change their health insurance.  In its second year as a state-based marketplace, Get Covered Illinois continues to deliver on its “Here to Help” mission by putting Illinoisans first.  The marketplace connects residents to coverage for the care they need, from routine checkups to ongoing treatment.

One way Illinoisans can make the most of open enrollment is by comparing plans to find coverage that meets their needs and budget.  Last year, people who shopped and compared plans saved an average of $150 a month on their premium.  With plans and prices changing each year, it’s important to review all options.  At GetCoveredIllinois.gov, Illinoisans can compare plans and estimated costs before creating an account or applying.  The website makes it easy to view premiums and deductibles, check prescription coverage and see whether preferred doctors and hospitals are in-network.  Get Covered Illinois is also the only place to apply for federal tax credits that lower the cost of coverage.

“The most important step returning customers can take is to review and compare the new plans available to them,” said Morgan Winters, Director of Get Covered Illinois.  “Do not assume last year’s plan is still the best fit.  Our licensed brokers can help you compare plans and prices and recommend a plan that fits your needs, at no cost to you.  Open enrollment is also the time to make sure the information on your application is up to date to ensure you get the correct financial help.”

Federal changes under H.R. 1 will affect some Illinoisans’ Medicaid and marketplace eligibility.  Last month, more than 9,000 lawfully present immigrants were kicked off Medicaid.  To help them avoid a gap in health insurance, Get Covered Illinois launched a special enrollment period offering retroactive coverage through December 31st.  Access to premium tax credits for this group will end on January 1st.

Get Covered Illinois is contacting impacted customers and encouraging them to carefully read their notices and reach out for help if they need it.  More information about these federal changes and when they take effect is available at GetCoveredIllinois.gov/MarketplaceChanges.

Get Covered Illinois certified navigators, trained professionals who provide free enrollment assistance, can guide Illinoisans through the application process, with support available in multiple languages.  Navigators are available to meet in person, online or over the phone in many communities across the state.  Navigators can also connect residents who are no longer eligible for Medicaid or marketplace financial help to free or low-cost health care in their community.

The annual Get Covered Illinois open enrollment period ends on January 15th.  Illinoisans who enroll by December 15th will have coverage starting January 1st.  Those who enroll by January 15th will have coverage starting February 1st.  To compare plans, enroll or find free help, visit GetCoveredIllinois.gov or call 1-866-311-1119 (TTY: 711).
